identity.description: Airtable: a no-code/low-code database and workflow platform (structured bases, tables, records, interfaces, automations), now positioned as a data layer for AI agents.
identity.identity_notes: Developer docs at airtable.com/developers describe the Airtable product (bases, records, OAuth integrations, MCP server). Product matches the assignment hint.

auth.oauth_flows: authorization_code and refresh_token grants at https://airtable.com/oauth2/v1/token (per OAuth reference error table). Access tokens expire after 60 minutes; refresh tokens valid 60 days.
auth.token_refresh: Refresh via https://airtable.com/oauth2/v1/token using refresh_token grant; no limit on refresh count as long as each refresh happens within the 60-day window. PATs do not expire by default.
auth.scopes_notes: PATs are created with scopes that control which API endpoints the token can use (e.g. schema.bases:read, data.records:read per community README). Enterprise scopes restricted to Enterprise Scale plans (search summary of support FAQ, not fetched directly).

access.production_restrictions: Not established. Enterprise-only: webhooks created with user API keys are restricted to Enterprise plan users and can no longer be created. Enterprise-scale scopes restricted to Enterprise Scale plans. Who may create OAuth integrations was not established.

write_ops: change base schema (via official MCP, by role)
api.rate_limits: 5 requests per second per base (REST API; webhook API shares the limit)
api.limitations: Official REST API resource list was not confirmed from fetched API intro page; resource list drawn from community README and MCP docs. Webhooks created with PAT or OAuth tokens expire and are disabled after 7 days. Webhook payloads contain only base ID, webhook ID, and timestamp; changes must be fetched separately. Official MCP does not appear to be a full admin API.
